title: The Thief Who Thought He Died

characters.name: The Thief Brahmin
characters.description: a gaunt, shifty-eyed Brahmin with a scraggly beard and a worn saffron dhoti; speaks with an oily, flattering smile

characters.name: Head Brahmin
characters.description: a wise, elder Brahmin with silver hair and a neat grey beard; calm eyes and an upright posture

characters.name: Young Brahmin
characters.description: a middle-aged Brahmin with a dark brown beard and anxious, watchful eyes

scenes.narration: In a quiet town lived a Brahmin known far and wide as a thief.
Four Brahmins arrived to sell their wares, earning a small purse of coins.
The thief slipped in as a friend, quoting the sacred texts with honeyed words.

dialogue.speaker: Thief Brahmin
dialogue.line: Your wisdom shines like the morning sun, honoured sages.

scenes.narration: Trusting him, they made him their travelling helper and guide.

dialogue.speaker: Head Brahmin
dialogue.line: You shall be our helper on this journey, good sir.

scenes.narration: They sold all their goods and bought glittering jewels with the coins.
Cutting their thighs, they hid the jewels inside and healed the wounds with ointment.
The thief saw everything and locked the hiding place in his mind.

dialogue.speaker: Thief Brahmin
dialogue.line: (to himself) The jewels are sewn into their very flesh. Tonight, I take them all.

scenes.narration: That night by the fire, the wise Head Brahmin read the thief's greedy heart.

dialogue.speaker: Head Brahmin
dialogue.line: (aside) This one plots harm. Let us teach him a lesson he will never forget.

scenes.narration: They slipped a sleeping draught into his food, and he sank into deep sleep.
They bound him, dragged him to the town gate, and left him in a muddy ditch.
Waking, half-deaf with fear, he swore he had died and been judged for his crimes.

dialogue.speaker: Thief Brahmin
dialogue.line: (waking in terror) I am dead! The gods have punished me for my theft!

scenes.narration: From that day he never stole again, for he feared the truth of his own soul.
